item.title: Free Law Classes Launch Monday at Sanders Beach Community Center
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola residents will have a chance to learn about the legal system at no cost, starting this coming Monday. item.content:encoded:
Pensacola residents will have a chance to learn about the legal system at no cost, starting this coming Monday. The People's Law School, hosted by the law firm Levin Papantonio, kicks off Sept. 14 at Sanders Beach Community Center with classes running from 6 to 8 p.m.

According to WKRG News 5, the program will hold classes every Monday throughout September, giving locals the opportunity to gain practical knowledge about legal matters that affect their daily lives.

The free educational initiative is designed to make legal information accessible to the broader Pensacola community. For residents interested in attending, classes will be held at the Sanders Beach Community Center location during the evening hours.

item.content:encoded: Hurlburt Field has rescheduled planned detonations that were originally set for today, according to Air Force officials. The base typically provides advance notice of such operations to minimize disruption to nearby communities.

item.content:encoded:
The Foley City Council has enacted a temporary halt on new data center applications, according to WKRG News 5. The measure passed its final reading during the council's Sept. 8 meeting, imposing a six-month moratorium on accepting or approving any new data center projects in the city.

The moratorium gives city officials time to review existing policies and potentially develop new regulations governing how data centers operate within Foley's limits. Data center projects have become increasingly common across the Southeast, raising questions about infrastructure impacts, power demands, and community concerns.

While Foley is just across the state line in Alabama, the decision could have implications for broader regional development patterns. The moratorium will remain in effect for six months unless the council votes to extend or lift it sooner.

item.title: Tate Volleyball Falls to Spanish Fort in Straight Sets

item.content:encoded:
The Tate High School Aggies couldn't keep their momentum rolling Wednesday evening, dropping a straight-sets match to visiting Spanish Fort High School in Cantonment. The Toros dominated the contest, winning 25-14, 25-20, 25-14 in what marked a quick turnaround for the Aggies after a strong performance the night before.

Tate had been riding high after picking up a 3-1 victory over Booker T. Washington on Tuesday, but the team ran into a tough test against the Alabama-based Spanish Fort squad. The Toros came into Escambia County and controlled play throughout the evening, showing little struggle in any of the three sets.

The loss drops Tate's record and sets up another opportunity to bounce back in upcoming matches as the volleyball season continues.
